name: Afghanistan
about: Afghanistan is a mountainous, landlocked country in South and Central Asia, crossed by the high Hindu Kush range. For centuries it sat on the Silk Road between Persia, India and China, and its valleys hold ruins from many empires. It is known for its carpets, pomegranates and the deep blue lapis lazuli mined in its mountains. Snow leopards still roam its remote northeast.
standout: Afghanistan's city of Balkh was one of the world's earliest centres of Zoroastrianism and is often called the "Mother of Cities".
did_you_know: The Wakhan Corridor, a thin strip of Afghanistan, reaches all the way to China. | Lapis lazuli from Badakhshan was used in Egypt's ancient treasures. | Buzkashi, played on horseback with a goat carcass, is a traditional national sport.

name: Angola
about: Angola lies on Africa's southwest coast, with a long Atlantic shoreline, high plateaus and dry deserts in the south. It is rich in oil and diamonds. Its capital, Luanda, is one of Africa's fastest-growing cities. Kizomba and semba music and dance come from Angola.
standout: Kalandula Falls is one of Africa's largest waterfalls by volume.
did_you_know: The giant sable antelope is found only in Angola. | Portuguese is the official language. | Part of the Namib Desert reaches into southern Angola.

name: Albania
about: Albania is a small country on the Balkan Peninsula, with a coast on the Adriatic and Ionian Seas. Mountains cover much of its land, and its beaches are some of Europe's least crowded. Its ancient city of Butrint holds Greek, Roman and Venetian ruins. Albanians nod to say no and shake their heads to say yes.
standout: Albania built over 170,000 concrete bunkers during the Cold War, more per area than almost any country.
did_you_know: The Albanian flag shows a black double-headed eagle. | Mother Teresa was ethnically Albanian. | Albanian is a branch of its own in the Indo-European language family.

name: Andorra
about: Andorra is a tiny country high in the Pyrenees, between France and Spain. Its valleys are popular for skiing in winter and hiking in summer. It has two co-princes: the President of France and a Spanish bishop. Andorra la Vella is the highest capital city in Europe.
standout: Andorra is the only country where Catalan is the sole official language.
did_you_know: Andorra has no airport. | Andorra la Vella sits at about 1,023 m. | It has one of the highest life expectancies in the world.

name: United Arab Emirates
about: The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates on the Arabian Peninsula, along the Persian Gulf. Desert covers most of the land, but cities like Dubai and Abu Dhabi are filled with skyscrapers and huge malls. Oil turned small fishing and pearl-diving towns into global hubs. Camel racing and falconry are cherished traditions.
standout: Burj Khalifa in Dubai, at 828 m, is the world's tallest building.
did_you_know: Most people living in the UAE were born in other countries. | The Palm Jumeirah is an artificial island shaped like a palm tree. | Pearl diving was the main industry before oil was found.

name: Argentina
about: Argentina stretches down the southern half of South America, from subtropical forests in the north to the icy tip of Tierra del Fuego. In between lie the high Andes, the grassy Pampas and the glaciers of Patagonia. Buenos Aires, its capital, is known for tango and grand old cafés. Argentine beef, football and dinosaur fossils are famous around the world.
standout: Aconcagua, at 6,961 m, is the highest mountain outside Asia.
did_you_know: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest mountain outside Asia. | Argentina is named after the Latin word for silver, argentum. | The tango was born in Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 1800s.

name: Armenia
about: Armenia is a small, mountainous, landlocked country in the South Caucasus. It has one of the oldest Christian traditions in the world, with stone monasteries perched on cliffs. Mount Ararat, a symbol of the nation, is visible from its capital, Yerevan. Apricots and lavash flatbread are part of its identity.
standout: Armenia became the first country to adopt Christianity as its state religion, in 301.
did_you_know: The Armenian alphabet was created around 405 by Mesrop Mashtots. | The world's oldest known leather shoe, about 5,500 years old, was found in an Armenian cave. | Yerevan is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
about: Antigua and Barbuda is a Caribbean nation of two main islands and many smaller ones. It is famous for white beaches and clear water. Nelson's Dockyard is a restored 18th-century naval base. Barbuda has a big frigatebird colony.
standout: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
did_you_know: Barbuda's frigatebird colony is one of the largest. | Sailing Week is a famous regatta. | Cricket is very popular.

name: Australia
about: Australia is both a country and a continent, set between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, and includes the island of Tasmania. Most people live along the coast, while the vast dry interior is known as the Outback. It is famous for Sydney's Opera House, Uluru and the Great Barrier Reef. Kangaroos, koalas and platypuses are found naturally nowhere else.
standout: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, visible from space.
did_you_know: Australia is the only country that covers an entire continent's mainland. | The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on Earth. | Voting in Australian federal elections is compulsory.

name: Austria
about: Austria is a landlocked country in Central Europe, two-thirds of it covered by the Alps. It was the centre of the Habsburg empire for centuries. Vienna is famous for palaces, coffee houses and classical music. Mozart was born in Salzburg.
standout: Vienna's Schönbrunn Zoo, founded in 1752, is the oldest zoo still running in the world.
did_you_know: The Eisriesenwelt is the largest known ice cave in the world. | The croissant may trace its roots to the Austrian kipferl. | Austria hosts a famous New Year's Day concert broadcast worldwide.

name: Azerbaijan
about: Azerbaijan sits between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains, where Eastern Europe meets Western Asia. Baku, its capital, mixes a walled old town with modern glass towers. It was one of the first places in the world to drill for oil industrially. Its name is often linked to fire, and flames burn naturally on Yanar Dag hillside.
standout: Azerbaijan has nearly half of the world's mud volcanoes.
did_you_know: Yanar Dag is a hillside where natural gas has burned for centuries. | Baku lies below sea level. | The Flame Towers are three skyscrapers shaped like flames.

name: Burundi
about: Burundi is a small, landlocked country in East Africa's Great Lakes region. Green hills cover most of its land, and Lake Tanganyika lies along its west. Its royal drummers are famous for powerful performances. Coffee and tea are its main exports.
standout: Lake Tanganyika, on Burundi's border, is the world's second-deepest lake.
did_you_know: The Royal Drum ritual is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. | Burundi is one of the most densely populated countries in Africa. | One of the southernmost sources of the Nile is in Burundi.

name: Belgium
about: Belgium is a small country in Western Europe on the North Sea, with three official languages: Dutch, French and German. Its cities, like Bruges and Ghent, have canals and medieval squares. It is famous for chocolate, waffles and fries. Brussels is home to the main institutions of the European Union.
standout: Belgium is home to one of the largest comic strip traditions in the world, including Tintin and the Smurfs.
did_you_know: Belgium makes hundreds of thousands of tonnes of chocolate a year. | The saxophone was invented by Belgian Adolphe Sax. | Belgium has over 1,000 kinds of beer.

name: Benin
about: Benin is a narrow country in West Africa, stretching from the coast north to the Niger River. It was the home of the Kingdom of Dahomey. Ganvié, a village built on stilts in a lake, is home to thousands. Vodun is celebrated on a national holiday.
standout: Benin is the birthplace of the Vodun (voodoo) religion.
did_you_know: Ganvié is one of the largest lake villages in Africa. | Benin celebrates a national Vodun day each January. | The Dahomey Amazons were a famous all-female army.

name: Burkina Faso
about: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa. Its name means "land of upright people". It is known for mud-brick architecture and painted houses in Tiébélé. Ouagadougou hosts a big African film festival.
standout: Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival.
did_you_know: Tiébélé's houses are painted with geometric patterns. | FESPACO is held every two years. | Burkina Faso is a major cotton producer.

name: Bangladesh
about: Bangladesh lies on the huge delta where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers meet the Bay of Bengal. It is one of the most densely populated countries on Earth, with green rice fields and hundreds of rivers. It is known for its textiles, rickshaws and Bengali poetry. Royal Bengal tigers swim between the islands of its mangrove forest.
standout: Bangladesh's Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with India.
did_you_know: Cox's Bazar has one of the longest unbroken natural sea beaches in the world, about 120 km. | International Mother Language Day, 21 February, began with Bangladesh's Bengali language movement. | Bangladesh is one of the world's largest makers of ready-made clothes.

name: Bulgaria
about: Bulgaria lies in southeastern Europe, with a Black Sea coast in the east and mountains across its middle and south. Its Rose Valley grows roses for a large share of the world's rose oil. It has ancient Thracian tombs and colourful monasteries like Rila. Bulgarian yoghurt is famous for its special bacteria.
standout: Bulgaria is home to the Cyrillic script's early development, at the Preslav and Ohrid schools.
did_you_know: Lactobacillus bulgaricus, a yoghurt bacterium, is named after Bulgaria. | Bulgaria produces a large share of the world's rose oil. | The Varna gold treasure is among the oldest worked gold in the world.

name: Bahrain
about: Bahrain is a small island country in the Persian Gulf, made up of one main island and around 30 smaller ones. It was once the centre of the ancient Dilmun civilisation and of pearl diving. Today it is a banking centre linked to Saudi Arabia by a long causeway. Bahrain hosts a Formula 1 Grand Prix.
standout: The Tree of Life in Bahrain is a 400-year-old tree growing alone in the desert.
did_you_know: The King Fahd Causeway is about 25 km long. | Bahrain has thousands of ancient burial mounds. | Its name means "two seas" in Arabic.

name: Bahamas
about: The Bahamas is a chain of about 700 islands in the Atlantic, near Florida. Its shallow seas glow turquoise. Pig Beach has swimming pigs. Junkanoo is a colourful street festival.
standout: Dean's Blue Hole is one of the deepest known blue holes in the world, about 200 m deep.
did_you_know: Swimming pigs live on Big Major Cay. | Andros Barrier Reef is one of the largest. | Pink sand beaches are on Harbour Island.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
about: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a mountainous country in the Balkans, with just a tiny strip of coast on the Adriatic. Rivers like the Neretva cut through green valleys and old stone towns. Sarajevo, its capital, mixes mosques, churches and synagogues. Ćevapi, small grilled sausages, are its best-loved food.
standout: The Stari Most bridge in Mostar, first built in 1566 and rebuilt in 2004, is famous for its divers.
did_you_know: Divers have jumped from Mostar's old bridge for centuries. | Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics. | Its coastline is only about 20 km long.

name: Belarus
about: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, mostly flat and covered in forests, marshes and lakes. It has thousands of lakes and is sometimes called "the land of blue lakes". Its capital, Minsk, was rebuilt after the Second World War. European bison live in its forests.
standout: Belovezhskaya Pushcha, shared with Poland, is one of Europe's last primeval forests.
did_you_know: Belarus has more than 10,000 lakes. | Potatoes are central to Belarusian cooking. | Mir Castle is a UNESCO-listed medieval fortress.

name: Belize
about: Belize is on the Caribbean coast of Central America. It has Maya ruins, jungle and a barrier reef. English is its official language. The Great Blue Hole is a famous dive site.
standout: Belize's barrier reef is the second-largest in the world.
did_you_know: The Great Blue Hole is about 300 m wide. | English is official. | Cockscomb Basin protects jaguars.

name: Bolivia
about: Bolivia is a landlocked country in South America, with the Andes and the Amazon. Salar de Uyuni becomes a giant mirror when wet. La Paz is the highest seat of government. Lake Titicaca lies on its border.
standout: Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world.
did_you_know: La Paz is the highest seat of government. | Uyuni holds lithium. | Lake Titicaca is a high navigable lake.

name: Brazil
about: Brazil covers almost half of South America, from the Amazon rainforest in the north to wide grasslands and long Atlantic beaches in the south. It is famous for football, samba and the Carnival in Rio de Janeiro. Most Brazilians speak Portuguese, which makes Brazil the largest Portuguese-speaking country. Its wetlands, the Pantanal, are among the best places on Earth to see jaguars in the wild.
standout: Brazil holds most of the Amazon, the world's largest tropical rainforest.
did_you_know: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador. | About 60% of the Amazon rainforest lies inside Brazil. | Brasília was built from scratch and became the capital in 1960.

name: Barbados
about: Barbados is the easternmost Caribbean island. It has beaches, coral reefs and sugar-cane fields. Cricket is a national passion. It became a republic in 2021.
standout: Barbados is considered the birthplace of rum.
did_you_know: Rihanna was born in Barbados. | Crop Over is a festival marking the end of the sugar harvest. | Harrison's Cave has stalactites.

name: Brunei
about: Brunei is a small, wealthy country on the north coast of the island of Borneo, split into two parts by Malaysia. Most of it is covered by tropical rainforest. Oil and gas made it rich, and its sultan's palace is one of the largest homes in the world. Proboscis monkeys live in its mangroves.
standout: Kampong Ayer in Brunei is one of the largest water villages in the world, built on stilts.
did_you_know: Brunei's full name means "Abode of Peace". | Its people pay no personal income tax. | Istana Nurul Iman, the sultan's palace, has around 1,800 rooms.

name: Bhutan
about: Bhutan is a small mountain kingdom in the eastern Himalayas, between India and China. Most of it is covered by forest, and its valleys are dotted with fortress-monasteries called dzongs. It limits tourism to protect its culture and nature. Bhutan is known for measuring success by its people's happiness, not just its wealth.
standout: Gangkhar Puensum, at 7,570 m, is the world's highest unclimbed mountain.
did_you_know: Bhutan measures progress with Gross National Happiness. | Bhutan is carbon negative: its forests absorb more CO₂ than the country emits. | Its constitution requires at least 60% of the land to stay forested.

name: Botswana
about: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, much of it covered by the Kalahari. The Okavango Delta floods each year and draws wildlife. It has one of the largest elephant populations. Diamonds have made it one of Africa's success stories.
standout: The Okavango Delta is one of the largest inland deltas in the world.
did_you_know: Botswana has the most elephants in Africa. | The Okavango floods during the dry season. | The Makgadikgadi salt pans are vast.

name: Central African Republic
about: The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in the heart of Africa. Its south is rainforest, its north is grassy savanna. It is home to forest elephants, gorillas and many bird species. Its capital, Bangui, lies on the Ubangi River.
standout: Dzanga-Sangha's forest clearing draws large gatherings of forest elephants.
did_you_know: Sango is a national language alongside French. | Forest elephants gather at mineral-rich clearings. | It is one of the least densely populated countries in Africa.

name: Canada
about: Canada covers the northern half of North America, from the Atlantic to the Pacific and up into the Arctic. Most Canadians live in a narrow band near the US border, leaving huge areas of forest, lakes and tundra almost empty. It is known for the Rocky Mountains, Niagara Falls and ice hockey. Polar bears roam the shores of Hudson Bay in the far north.
standout: Canada has more lakes than any other country, with over half of the world's large lakes.
did_you_know: Canada has the longest coastline of any country. | Canada holds roughly a fifth of the world's fresh surface water. | Canada has two official languages, English and French.

name: Switzerland
about: Switzerland is a landlocked, mountainous country in Central Europe, with the Alps covering most of it. It has four national languages and is famous for neutrality. Swiss watches, chocolate and cheese are known worldwide. The Matterhorn is one of its best-known peaks.
standout: The Gotthard Base Tunnel, 57 km long, is the world's longest railway tunnel.
did_you_know: Switzerland has about 1,500 lakes. | The World Wide Web was invented at CERN, near Geneva. | Voters decide many national questions directly in referendums.

name: Chile
about: Chile is a long, narrow country squeezed between the Andes and the Pacific along South America's western edge. Its north holds the Atacama Desert, its centre has vineyards and Santiago, and its south breaks into fjords, glaciers and Patagonia. It also owns remote Easter Island with its giant moai statues. Clear desert skies make Chile a world centre for astronomy.
standout: Chile's Atacama Desert hosts ALMA, one of the world's largest radio telescope arrays.
did_you_know: Chile is about 4,300 km long but on average only about 175 km wide. | The Atacama Desert is one of the driest non-polar places on Earth. | Chile produces more copper than any other country.

name: China
about: China covers a huge part of East Asia, from the Himalayas and deserts in the west to busy coastal cities in the east. It is one of the world's oldest continuous civilisations and its most populous country after India. Paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass were all invented there. Giant pandas live in its bamboo forests.
standout: The Great Wall of China, built over many centuries, stretches for thousands of kilometres.
did_you_know: China officially uses a single time zone for the whole country. | The Three Gorges Dam is the world's largest power station by capacity. | China grows more tea than any other country.

name: Ivory Coast
about: Côte d'Ivoire, or Ivory Coast, is on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa. It has beaches, rainforests and savanna. Abidjan is its largest city, and Yamoussoukro has one of the largest churches in the world. It grows a large share of the world's cocoa.
standout: Côte d'Ivoire is the world's largest cocoa producer.
did_you_know: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is one of the largest churches in the world. | Côte d'Ivoire grows about 40% of the world's cocoa. | Taï National Park has pygmy hippos.

name: Cameroon
about: Cameroon is in Central Africa, with beaches, rainforests, mountains and savanna. It is often called "Africa in miniature" because it has almost every type of African landscape. It has over 250 languages. Football is a national passion.
standout: Mount Cameroon is one of Africa's most active volcanoes and among the wettest places on Earth.
did_you_know: Debundscha, near Mount Cameroon, is one of the rainiest places on Earth. | Both English and French are official languages. | Cameroon's national football team are known as the Indomitable Lions.

name: DR Congo
about: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is the second-largest country in Africa, covered largely by the Congo rainforest. The Congo River curves through its heart. It is home to gorillas, okapis and bonobos. It is rich in minerals like cobalt and copper.
standout: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, over 220 m deep in places.
did_you_know: Bonobos, close relatives of humans, live only in the DR Congo. | The okapi looks like a zebra but is related to the giraffe. | The DR Congo produces much of the world's cobalt.

name: Republic of the Congo
about: The Republic of the Congo sits on the equator in Central Africa, with rainforests, rivers and a short Atlantic coast. Its capital, Brazzaville, faces Kinshasa across the Congo River. It is home to gorillas and chimpanzees. Congolese rumba music is famous across Africa.
standout: Odzala-Kokoua National Park is a stronghold of western lowland gorillas.
did_you_know: Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the closest pair of capital cities in the world. | About two-thirds of the country is forest. | Congolese rumba is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.

name: Colombia
about: Colombia is in northwest South America, with coasts on two oceans. It has the Andes, Amazon and Caribbean beaches. It is known for coffee and flowers. Caño Cristales river turns rainbow-coloured.
standout: Colombia has more bird species than any other country.
did_you_know: Colombia has nearly 2,000 bird species. | Caño Cristales is the "river of five colours". | Colombia grows famous coffee.

name: Comoros
about: The Comoros is a group of volcanic islands in the Indian Ocean, between Mozambique and Madagascar. Its islands have beaches, forests and an active volcano, Mount Karthala. It is a major producer of ylang-ylang, used in perfume. Arabic, French and Comorian are spoken.
standout: The coelacanth, a fish thought extinct for 66 million years, was rediscovered near the Comoros.
did_you_know: Mount Karthala has one of the largest active volcanic craters. | Comoros is a major source of ylang-ylang oil. | Its name comes from the Arabic for "moon".

name: Cape Verde
about: Cape Verde is a group of ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic, west of Senegal. Its islands range from desert-like to green and mountainous. Its music, especially morna, is famous. Fogo island has an active volcano.
standout: Cape Verde's morna music is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
did_you_know: Cesária Évora made morna famous worldwide. | Fogo's volcano last erupted in 2014. | Cape Verde was uninhabited before the Portuguese arrived.

name: Costa Rica
about: Costa Rica is a Central American country with rainforests, volcanoes and two coasts. A quarter of its land is protected. It abolished its army in 1948. Sloths and toucans live in its forests.
standout: Costa Rica has about 5% of the world's species in only 0.03% of its land.
did_you_know: Costa Rica has no army. | It runs on mostly renewable electricity. | "Pura vida" is a common phrase.

name: Cuba
about: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean. Havana has colourful colonial streets. Its music, like salsa and son, is known worldwide. Cigars and sugar cane are traditional products.
standout: Cuba is famous for its classic 1950s American cars still in daily use.
did_you_know: The bee hummingbird, the smallest bird, lives in Cuba. | Old Havana is a UNESCO site. | Cuba has very high literacy.

name: Cyprus
about: Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean, south of Türkiye. Its sunny coast, mountains and old villages draw many visitors. It has ancient Greek, Roman and medieval ruins. Halloumi cheese comes from here.
standout: Cyprus is the mythical birthplace of Aphrodite, the Greek goddess of love.
did_you_know: Halloumi cheese originated in Cyprus. | Cyprus has one of the oldest wines still made, Commandaria. | The island was a source of copper in ancient times.

name: Czechia
about: Czechia is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with hills, forests and old castles. Its capital, Prague, has a medieval astronomical clock and many bridges. It is known for glassmaking and beer. Czechs drink more beer per person than any other nation.
standout: Prague Castle is one of the largest ancient castle complexes in the world.
did_you_know: Prague's astronomical clock is the oldest still working in the world. | The word "robot" first appeared in a Czech play in 1920. | Czechia has more than 2,000 castles and chateaux.

name: Germany
about: Germany sits in the middle of Europe, from the North and Baltic Seas down to the Alps. Its cities, like Berlin, Munich and Hamburg, mix old castles and cathedrals with modern design. It is known for its cars, beer festivals and Christmas markets. Composers such as Bach and Beethoven were born here.
standout: Karl Benz built the first practical petrol-powered car in Germany in 1885.
did_you_know: Germany borders nine countries, more than any other in Europe except Russia. | The printing press with movable type was developed in Mainz around 1440. | Germany has more than 20,000 castles.

name: Djibouti
about: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa, at the entrance to the Red Sea. It is hot and dry, with salt lakes and volcanic landscapes. Its port is one of the busiest in the region. Whale sharks gather in its waters each winter.
standout: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, about 155 m below sea level.
did_you_know: Lake Assal is one of the saltiest lakes in the world. | Lac Abbé has limestone chimneys that release steam. | Whale sharks gather in the Gulf of Tadjoura.

name: Dominica
about: Dominica is a mountainous Caribbean island covered in rainforest. It has hot springs, waterfalls and a boiling lake. It is called the "Nature Island". It is home to the Kalinago people.
standout: Dominica's Boiling Lake is one of the largest hot lakes in the world.
did_you_know: Dominica has many rivers. | Sperm whales live year-round off its coast. | The Sisserou parrot is on its flag.

name: Denmark
about: Denmark is a small Nordic country made up of the Jutland peninsula and more than 400 islands. No place is far from the sea. It is known for Vikings, bicycles and the idea of "hygge", meaning cosiness. It also governs Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
standout: LEGO bricks were invented in Denmark, and the name comes from the Danish "leg godt", meaning "play well".
did_you_know: Denmark's flag is one of the oldest national flags still in use. | Copenhagen has more bikes than cars. | Hans Christian Andersen, author of famous fairy tales, was Danish.

name: Dominican Republic
about: The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti. It has the highest peak and lowest point in the Caribbean. Merengue and bachata music come from here. Baseball is hugely popular.
standout: Santo Domingo has the oldest cathedral in the Americas, completed in 1541.
did_you_know: Pico Duarte is the Caribbean's highest peak. | Lake Enriquillo is below sea level. | Many top baseball players come from here.

name: Algeria
about: Algeria is in North Africa, with a Mediterranean coast and the Sahara covering most of its land. Its Tassili n'Ajjer plateau has ancient rock art. Roman ruins stand at Timgad and Djémila. Couscous is a national dish.
standout: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
did_you_know: Over 80% of Algeria is desert. | Tassili n'Ajjer rock art is thousands of years old. | Timgad is a well-preserved Roman town.

name: Ecuador
about: Ecuador sits on the equator in South America. It has the Andes, Amazon and the Galápagos Islands. Quito is a high capital. Its name means "equator".
standout: The Galápagos Islands inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.
did_you_know: Chimborazo's summit is the farthest point from Earth's centre. | Panama hats come from Ecuador. | Galápagos tortoises live very long.

name: Egypt
about: Egypt sits in the northeast corner of Africa, with the Sinai Peninsula reaching into Asia. Almost all of it is desert, so nearly everyone lives along the green strip of the Nile and its delta. Ancient Egyptians built the pyramids, the Sphinx and the temples of Luxor thousands of years ago. The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Seas through Egypt.
standout: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
did_you_know: About 95% of Egyptians live within a few kilometres of the Nile. | The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years. | Egypt spans two continents, with the Sinai Peninsula in Asia.

name: Eritrea
about: Eritrea is on the Horn of Africa, along the Red Sea coast. Its highlands are cool, while the Danakil Depression is one of the hottest places on Earth. Asmara, its capital, has art deco cafés and cinemas. The Dahlak Archipelago has coral reefs.
standout: Asmara is known for one of the world's largest collections of modernist buildings from the early 1900s.
did_you_know: Asmara is a UNESCO World Heritage city. | Eritrea has nine recognised ethnic groups. | The Danakil area is one of the hottest places on Earth.

name: Spain
about: Spain covers most of the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe, plus the Balearic and Canary Islands. It is known for sunny beaches, flamenco dancing and grand buildings like the Alhambra. Its many regions have their own languages and food. Spanish is spoken by hundreds of millions of people worldwide.
standout: Barcelona's Sagrada Família has been under construction since 1882.
did_you_know: Spain produces about half of the world's olive oil. | Madrid's Sobrino de Botín is often called the world's oldest restaurant. | The Canary Islands are much closer to Africa than to mainland Spain.

name: Estonia
about: Estonia is a small Baltic country on the Gulf of Finland, with forests, bogs and over 2,000 islands. Tallinn, its capital, has a well-preserved medieval old town. It is one of the most digital countries in the world. Estonians are known for big song festivals.
standout: Estonia was the first country to offer online voting in a national election, in 2007.
did_you_know: Skype was developed by engineers in Estonia. | About half of Estonia is covered by forest. | Estonia offers e-residency to people anywhere in the world.

name: Ethiopia
about: Ethiopia is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa, with high mountains, deep valleys and the Rift Valley. It was never colonised for long and has its own ancient alphabet and calendar. It is believed to be the birthplace of coffee. Lalibela has churches carved out of solid rock.
standout: "Lucy", one of the most famous early human ancestor fossils, was found in Ethiopia.
did_you_know: Ethiopia's calendar has 13 months. | Coffee is thought to have first been found in Ethiopia. | Lalibela's rock-hewn churches date from around 1200.

name: Finland
about: Finland is a Nordic country in northern Europe, covered by forests and lakes. In the far north, Lapland has reindeer and the midnight sun. Saunas are part of everyday life. Finland often tops world happiness rankings.
standout: Finland has around 188,000 lakes, earning it the name "land of a thousand lakes".
did_you_know: There are about as many saunas as cars in Finland. | Linux was created by Finnish student Linus Torvalds. | Finland is one of the world's most forested countries.

name: Fiji
about: Fiji is a group of over 300 islands in the South Pacific. It has coral reefs, rainforests and beaches. Rugby sevens is hugely popular. Bula is a common greeting.
standout: Fiji's Great Astrolabe Reef is one of the largest barrier reefs in the world.
did_you_know: Fiji has won Olympic gold in rugby sevens. | Kava is a traditional drink. | About a third of its islands are inhabited.

name: France
about: France lies in Western Europe between the Atlantic, the English Channel and the Mediterranean, and also includes overseas regions in the Caribbean, South America and the Indian Ocean. It is known for Paris, the Alps, vineyards and castles along the Loire. French cooking, fashion and art have shaped tastes around the world. Every July, the Tour de France bike race loops around the country.
standout: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.
did_you_know: Counting its overseas regions, France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country. | French Guiana in South America is part of France and uses the euro. | France is the most visited country in the world.

name: Micronesia
about: The Federated States of Micronesia is a nation of over 600 islands in the western Pacific. It has four states. Nan Madol is an ancient stone city. Yap has huge stone money.
standout: Nan Madol is a ruined city built on artificial islets.
did_you_know: Yap uses giant stone discs as money. | Nan Madol is built on reefs. | It has many languages.

name: Gabon
about: Gabon sits on the equator on Africa's Atlantic coast, and nearly nine-tenths of it is rainforest. It protects a large share of its land as national parks. Forest elephants, gorillas and leopards live in its forests. Its capital is Libreville.
standout: Gabon's Loango National Park is known for elephants, hippos and buffalo walking on the beach.
did_you_know: Gabon has about 88% forest cover. | Hippos sometimes swim in the sea off Loango. | The Oklo natural nuclear reactors formed in Gabon about 2 billion years ago.

name: United Kingdom
about: The United Kingdom is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, on islands off northwest Europe. London is one of the world's great cities. It is known for its royal family, castles and football. Shakespeare and the Beatles came from here.
standout: The World Wide Web was invented by British scientist Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.
did_you_know: Football, rugby and tennis rules were first written down in Britain. | No place in the UK is more than about 120 km from the sea. | Big Ben is the name of the bell, not the tower.

name: Georgia
about: Georgia lies in the Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the Caspian, with the Greater Caucasus mountains along its north. Its villages have ancient stone towers and churches. Georgians have their own alphabet and are famous for hospitality, polyphonic singing and feasts called supra. Khachapuri, cheese-filled bread, is a national favourite.
standout: Georgia has one of the oldest known winemaking traditions, going back about 8,000 years.
did_you_know: Georgian is written in one of only 14 unique alphabets in use today. | Wine is traditionally fermented in clay pots called qvevri, buried underground. | Ushguli is one of the highest permanently inhabited villages in Europe.

name: Ghana
about: Ghana lies on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa. It was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957. Its coast has old castles from the slave trade. Kente cloth and cocoa are famous.
standout: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest artificial lakes by area.
did_you_know: Ghana was formerly called the Gold Coast. | Kente cloth is woven in strips. | Ghana is one of the world's top cocoa producers.

name: Guinea
about: Guinea is on West Africa's Atlantic coast. Its highlands give rise to several major rivers. It has some of the world's largest bauxite reserves. Its music and drumming traditions are famous.
standout: Guinea's Fouta Djallon highlands are the source of the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers.
did_you_know: Guinea has huge bauxite deposits, used to make aluminium. | The Mount Nimba reserve has unique animals. | The djembe drum is linked to the region.

name: Gambia
about: The Gambia is a narrow country in West Africa, following the Gambia River inland. It is surrounded by Senegal except at its coast. Its riverbanks are full of birds. Kora music is a cherished tradition.
standout: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
did_you_know: The Gambia is almost entirely surrounded by Senegal. | It is a top birdwatching spot. | Kunta Kinteh Island is linked to the slave trade.

name: Guinea-Bissau
about: Guinea-Bissau is a small country on West Africa's coast, with mangroves and the Bijagós islands. Its islands have unique cultures and wildlife. Cashew nuts are its main export. Portuguese is the official language.
standout: The Bijagós Archipelago is home to saltwater hippos.
did_you_know: Bijagós hippos swim in the sea. | Cashews are the main export. | It has many sea turtle nesting beaches.

name: Equatorial Guinea
about: Equatorial Guinea is a small country on Central Africa's coast, made up of a mainland region and islands. Its capital, Malabo, is on Bioko Island. Rainforests and volcanic mountains cover its land. Oil has become its main industry.
standout: Equatorial Guinea is the only African country where Spanish is an official language.
did_you_know: Its island of Annobón is far out in the Atlantic. | Bioko Island is volcanic. | It is one of Africa's smallest countries.

name: Greece
about: Greece lies at the southern end of the Balkans, with about 6,000 islands in the Aegean and Ionian Seas. Ancient Greeks gave the world the Olympic Games, theatre and much of modern philosophy. Ruins like the Acropolis stand above its cities. Whitewashed villages with blue domes cover islands like Santorini.
standout: Ancient Greece was the birthplace of democracy, in Athens in the 5th century BCE.
did_you_know: The Olympic Games began in Olympia around 776 BCE. | No place in Greece is more than about 140 km from the sea. | Greek is one of the oldest recorded living languages.

name: Grenada
about: Grenada is a small Caribbean island country. It grows nutmeg, mace and cocoa. It has beaches and an underwater sculpture park. Nutmeg is on its flag.
standout: Grenada is known as the "Spice Isle" for its nutmeg.
did_you_know: Its underwater sculpture park was among the first. | Grenada's flag shows a nutmeg. | It is a major nutmeg exporter.

name: Guatemala
about: Guatemala is in Central America, with volcanoes, lakes and Maya ruins. Many people speak Maya languages. Lake Atitlán is ringed by volcanoes. Its textiles are colourful.
standout: Tikal was one of the largest cities of the ancient Maya.
did_you_know: Guatemala has over 20 Maya languages. | Lake Atitlán is very deep. | The quetzal bird gives its name to the currency.

name: Guyana
about: Guyana is on South America's north coast. Most of it is rainforest. English is its official language. Kaieteur Falls is a famous waterfall.
standout: Kaieteur Falls is one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world.
did_you_know: Guyana is the only English-speaking country in South America. | Giant water lilies grow there. | Kaieteur is about 226 m tall.

name: Honduras
about: Honduras is in Central America, with mountains, forests and a Caribbean coast. Its Bay Islands have coral reefs. Copán has Maya ruins. Whale sharks visit its waters.
standout: Copán is famous for having some of the finest carved Maya sculptures.
did_you_know: The Bay Islands are on the Mesoamerican Reef. | Copán's hieroglyphic stairway is very long. | Bananas were a key export.

name: Croatia
about: Croatia curves along the Adriatic Sea, with more than a thousand islands off its coast. Its walled city of Dubrovnik and Roman palace in Split draw visitors from everywhere. Inland, it has green hills, vineyards and the Plitvice Lakes. The necktie, or cravat, is named after Croatian soldiers.
standout: Plitvice Lakes is a chain of 16 lakes linked by waterfalls, built up by natural travertine barriers.
did_you_know: The word "cravat" comes from "Croat". | The Dalmatian dog is named after Croatia's Dalmatia region. | Hum is often called the smallest town in the world.

name: Haiti
about: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola. In 1804 it became the first country founded after a successful slave revolt. Its art and music are vibrant. Kreyòl is spoken alongside French.
standout: The Citadelle Laferrière is the largest fortress in the Americas.
did_you_know: Haiti was the first Black-led republic. | Its art is famous for colour. | Kreyòl is spoken by nearly all.

name: Hungary
about: Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe, split by the Danube River. Budapest is made of two cities, Buda and Pest, joined by bridges. It is famous for its thermal baths, paprika and Lake Balaton. Hungarian is unrelated to most of its neighbours' languages.
standout: Lake Hévíz is the largest thermal lake in the world that people can swim in.
did_you_know: The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian Ernő Rubik. | Budapest has more thermal springs than any other capital. | Hungarian belongs to the Uralic language family, related to Finnish.

name: Indonesia
about: Indonesia is a chain of more than 17,000 islands strung between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, including Java, Sumatra, Bali and parts of Borneo and New Guinea. It has hundreds of ethnic groups and languages, united by the Indonesian language. Volcanoes, rice terraces and coral reefs shape its landscapes. Rare animals like orangutans and Komodo dragons live in its forests.
standout: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago country.
did_you_know: Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands. | Indonesia has more active volcanoes than any other country. | Komodo dragons, the largest living lizards, live only in Indonesia.

name: India
about: India fills most of South Asia, running from the snowy Himalayas in the north to tropical beaches in the south, and includes the Andaman, Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands. It is the world's most populous country, home to ancient temples, the Taj Mahal and hundreds of languages. Its food, festivals like Diwali and Holi, and film industry are loved worldwide. Tigers, elephants and snow leopards all live within its borders.
standout: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, 182 m tall, is the world's tallest statue.
did_you_know: India has 22 languages listed in its constitution's Eighth Schedule. | Mawsynram in Meghalaya is often listed as one of the wettest inhabited places on Earth. | The game of chess grew out of chaturanga, played in India around the 6th century.

name: Ireland
about: Ireland is an island nation in the North Atlantic, west of Great Britain. Its green hills, cliffs and stone castles are famous. Irish music, dance and storytelling are loved across the world. The Cliffs of Moher rise over 200 m from the sea.
standout: Halloween traces its roots to Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival from Ireland.
did_you_know: Ireland has no native snakes. | The harp is a national symbol. | Saint Patrick's Day is celebrated in many countries.

name: Iran
about: Iran sits between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, a land of high plateaus, deserts and snowy mountains. It is home to one of the world's oldest civilisations, and its cities hold blue-tiled mosques, gardens and bazaars. Persian poetry, carpets and saffron are famous worldwide. In ancient times, Iranians built underground channels called qanats to carry water across the desert.
standout: Persepolis, built about 2,500 years ago, was the ceremonial capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire.
did_you_know: Iran grows most of the world's saffron. | The game of polo has deep roots in ancient Persia. | Nowruz, the Persian New Year, begins on the first day of spring.

name: Iraq
about: Iraq lies in the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, once known as Mesopotamia. It is often called a cradle of civilisation, where some of the first cities, laws and writing appeared. Babylon and Ur stood here. Its southern marshes are home to the Marsh Arabs, who build houses from reeds.
standout: Ancient Mesopotamia, in today's Iraq, is where cuneiform, one of the earliest writing systems, was invented.
did_you_know: The Code of Hammurabi, one of the earliest written law codes, comes from Babylon. | The wheel is thought to have been invented in Mesopotamia. | Baghdad was once one of the largest cities in the world.

name: Iceland
about: Iceland is an island in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle. It sits on top of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, so volcanoes, geysers and hot springs are everywhere. Glaciers, black-sand beaches and waterfalls cover its landscape. In winter, the northern lights often dance across its long, dark skies.
standout: Vatnajökull is Europe's largest glacier by volume.
did_you_know: Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930. | Almost all of Iceland's electricity comes from hydropower and geothermal energy. | Iceland has no standing army.

name: Israel
about: Israel lies on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, with deserts in the south and green hills in the north. It is home to sites holy to Judaism, Christianity and Islam, especially in Jerusalem. It is known for technology start-ups and farming in dry land. The Dead Sea is so salty that people float easily.
standout: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land point on Earth, about 430 m below sea level.
did_you_know: Drip irrigation was developed in Israel. | Hebrew was revived as an everyday spoken language in modern times. | The Dead Sea is almost ten times saltier than the ocean.

name: Italy
about: Italy is a boot-shaped peninsula in southern Europe, with the islands of Sicily and Sardinia. It was the heart of the Roman Empire and the birthplace of the Renaissance. Cities like Rome, Florence and Venice are full of art and history. Pizza and pasta are loved around the world.
standout: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
did_you_know: Two independent countries, San Marino and Vatican City, lie inside Italy. | Venice is built on more than 100 small islands. | Mount Etna in Sicily is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.

name: Jamaica
about: Jamaica is a Caribbean island with mountains, beaches and waterfalls. It is the birthplace of reggae. Its sprinters are among the world's fastest. Blue Mountain coffee is prized.
standout: Reggae music, made famous by Bob Marley, began in Jamaica.
did_you_know: Usain Bolt is from Jamaica. | Blue Mountain coffee is famous. | Jamaica has many rivers.

name: Jordan
about: Jordan is a country in Western Asia between the Mediterranean world and the Arabian desert. Most of it is dry desert, including the red sands of Wadi Rum. Its ancient city of Petra is carved into cliffs. It shares the Dead Sea, where visitors float on the salty water.
standout: Petra is a city carved into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs more than 2,000 years ago.
did_you_know: Jordan has only about 26 km of coastline, on the Gulf of Aqaba. | Wadi Rum has been used as a film location for scenes set on Mars. | Mansaf, lamb cooked in yoghurt sauce, is the national dish.

name: Japan
about: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, made up of four main islands and thousands of smaller ones. It mixes ancient temples and shrines with ultra-modern cities like Tokyo and Osaka. Its landscapes range from snowy northern mountains to subtropical beaches in Okinawa, and Mount Fuji is its best-known symbol. Japanese food, anime and bullet trains have fans all over the world.
standout: Japan opened the world's first high-speed railway, the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, in 1964.
did_you_know: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands. | Japan's imperial house is the oldest continuous hereditary monarchy in the world. | Around 70% of Japan is covered by mountains.

name: Kazakhstan
about: Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country, stretching across Central Asia from the Caspian Sea to China. Most of it is flat steppe, but snowy mountains rise in the southeast. Nomadic horse culture shapes its traditions. Apples are thought to have first grown in its mountain forests.
standout: Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan is the world's first and largest space launch site.
did_you_know: Yuri Gagarin, the first person in space, launched from Kazakhstan in 1961. | Almaty's name is linked to the Kazakh word for apple. | Astana, the capital, was built up rapidly after 1997.

name: Kenya
about: Kenya lies on the equator in East Africa, with Indian Ocean beaches on one side and Lake Victoria on the other. The Great Rift Valley cuts through its middle, and Mount Kenya rises over the highlands. It is famous for safaris in parks like the Maasai Mara. Each year, huge herds of wildebeest and zebra cross its plains in the Great Migration.
standout: Over a million wildebeest pass through Kenya's Maasai Mara in one of the world's largest animal migrations.
did_you_know: The equator runs through Kenya. | Kenya's M-Pesa was one of the first mobile money services used across a whole country. | Kenyan runners have won more Olympic medals in long-distance events than any other nation's.

name: Kyrgyzstan
about: Kyrgyzstan is a small, mountainous country in Central Asia, almost entirely covered by the Tian Shan range. Herders still take their animals to high summer pastures and live in yurts. Its people are known for the epic poem of Manas, one of the longest in the world. Snow leopards live in its peaks.
standout: Issyk-Kul is one of the largest mountain lakes in the world and never freezes despite its height.
did_you_know: The roof frame of a yurt appears on Kyrgyzstan's flag. | The Manas epic is hundreds of thousands of lines long. | The World Nomad Games have been held in Kyrgyzstan.

name: Cambodia
about: Cambodia lies in mainland Southeast Asia, with the Mekong River and the great Tonlé Sap lake at its heart. It was the centre of the Khmer Empire, which built hundreds of temples at Angkor. Rice fields, floating villages and the capital Phnom Penh shape the country. Angkor Wat even appears on the national flag.
standout: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest religious monument in the world.
did_you_know: The Tonlé Sap river reverses its flow every rainy season. | Cambodia's flag is one of very few that shows a building. | Khmer has one of the longest alphabets in the world.

name: Kiribati
about: Kiribati is a Pacific nation of 33 islands across the equator. Its islands are low atolls. It is one of the first places to see each new day. Phoenix Islands is a huge protected area.
standout: Kiritimati is one of the largest coral atolls by land area.
did_you_know: Kiribati spans four hemispheres. | It is among the first to see the New Year. | Phoenix Islands is a large marine reserve.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
about: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas. Its two volcanic islands have rainforest and beaches. Brimstone Hill fort is a UNESCO site. Green vervet monkeys live there.
standout: Brimstone Hill Fortress is one of the best-preserved fortresses in the Americas.
did_you_know: It is the smallest country in the Western Hemisphere. | Alexander Hamilton was born on Nevis. | Its scenic railway once carried sugar cane.

name: South Korea
about: South Korea occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia, with mountains covering much of its land. Seoul is a giant, high-tech city mixing palaces with skyscrapers. Korean pop music, films and food have become hugely popular worldwide. Jeju Island, off its south coast, is a volcanic island with lava tubes.
standout: Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was created in 1443 under King Sejong.
did_you_know: South Korea has some of the fastest internet speeds in the world. | Kimchi, fermented vegetables, is eaten at almost every Korean meal. | Taekwondo, a Korean martial art, is an Olympic sport.

name: Kuwait
about: Kuwait is a small desert country at the top of the Persian Gulf, between Iraq and Saudi Arabia. It sits on some of the world's largest oil reserves. Before oil, its people lived by trade, fishing and pearl diving. Summers are among the hottest anywhere, often over 50 °C.
standout: The Kuwait Towers, opened in 1979, have become the symbol of the country.
did_you_know: The Kuwaiti dinar is one of the highest-valued currencies in the world. | Kuwait has no permanent rivers or lakes. | Its summer temperatures are among the highest recorded on Earth.

name: Laos
about: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, shaped by forested mountains and the Mekong River. Its towns are quiet, with gold-roofed temples and monks walking at dawn to collect alms. Luang Prabang is a well-preserved royal city. The mysterious Plain of Jars holds thousands of ancient stone jars.
standout: Khone Phapheng on the Mekong is the largest waterfall in Southeast Asia by volume of water.
did_you_know: Laos is often called the most bombed country per person in history. | Sticky rice is eaten with almost every meal. | Nobody knows for sure what the giant stone jars were used for.

name: Lebanon
about: Lebanon is a small, mountainous country on the eastern Mediterranean coast. Its snowy peaks once held great cedar forests, and a cedar tree is on its flag. Ancient Phoenician cities like Byblos and Tyre were trading powers. Lebanese food, with dishes like tabbouleh and hummus, is loved across the world.
standout: The cedars of Lebanon are among the oldest trees mentioned in historical records.
did_you_know: Byblos is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. | You can ski and swim in the sea on the same day in spring. | The Phoenician alphabet, developed here, is an ancestor of many modern alphabets.

name: Liberia
about: Liberia is on West Africa's Atlantic coast, with rainforests and long beaches. Its capital, Monrovia, is named after US President James Monroe. It was Africa's first republic. Pygmy hippos live in its forests.
standout: Liberia was founded by freed slaves from the United States and became independent in 1847.
did_you_know: Liberia's flag looks like the US flag with one star. | Ellen Johnson Sirleaf was Africa's first elected female head of state. | Liberia has some of West Africa's largest remaining rainforests.

name: Libya
about: Libya is in North Africa, with Mediterranean coast and most land in the Sahara. It has Greek and Roman ruins. Most people live near the coast. Its desert holds big underground water reserves.
standout: Leptis Magna is one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the Mediterranean.
did_you_know: Libya has no permanent rivers. | The Great Man-Made River pipes water from desert aquifers. | Ghadames is an old desert town.

name: Saint Lucia
about: Saint Lucia is a mountainous Caribbean island. Its two Pitons rise from the sea. It has a drive-in volcano and hot springs. Two Nobel Prize winners came from it.
standout: The Pitons are two volcanic spires rising straight from the sea.
did_you_know: Saint Lucia has two Nobel laureates. | Sulphur Springs is a drive-in volcano. | Its national day honours Saint Lucy.

name: Liechtenstein
about: Liechtenstein is a tiny, doubly landlocked country in the Alps, between Switzerland and Austria. It is ruled by a prince who lives in a castle above the capital, Vaduz. Its people enjoy one of the highest incomes in the world. Hiking trails cross the whole country.
standout: Liechtenstein is one of the world's largest makers of false teeth.
did_you_know: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries. | It has no army. | You can walk across the whole country in a day.

name: Sri Lanka
about: Sri Lanka is a teardrop-shaped island in the Indian Ocean, just south of India. Its hill country is covered in tea gardens, while golden beaches circle the coast. It has ancient Buddhist cities, temples and some of the world's oldest written history. Elephants, leopards and blue whales can all be seen in and around the island.
standout: Sigiriya is a 5th-century palace built on top of a 200 m rock column.
did_you_know: Sri Lanka elected the world's first female prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike, in 1960. | Ceylon tea is named after the island's old name. | Sri Lanka is one of the best places on Earth to spot blue whales.

name: Lesotho
about: Lesotho is a mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa. It has the highest low point of any country. Its people wear woollen blankets and conical hats. Maletsunyane Falls drops nearly 200 m.
standout: Lesotho is the only country entirely above 1,000 m in elevation.
did_you_know: Lesotho's lowest point is about 1,400 m. | The Basotho hat is a symbol. | It is one of only three countries entirely surrounded by another.

name: Lithuania
about: Lithuania is the largest of the three Baltic states, with forests, lakes and a sandy coast. The Curonian Spit has some of Europe's highest moving dunes. Vilnius has a baroque old town. Basketball is its national passion.
standout: Lithuanian is one of the oldest living Indo-European languages, close to ancient Sanskrit in some ways.
did_you_know: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, in 1990. | The Hill of Crosses has more than 100,000 crosses. | Basketball is often called Lithuania's second religion.

name: Luxembourg
about: Luxembourg is a small, landlocked country in Western Europe, between Belgium, France and Germany. It is the world's last grand duchy. Its capital is built on cliffs over deep river gorges. It is a major centre for banking and EU institutions.
standout: Luxembourg was the first country to make all public transport free, in 2020.
did_you_know: Luxembourgish, French and German are all official languages. | It has one of the highest incomes per person in the world. | Luxembourg City's old quarters sit on steep rock fortifications.

name: Latvia
about: Latvia is a Baltic country with forests, rivers and a long sandy coast. Riga, its capital, has one of the largest collections of art nouveau buildings anywhere. It has thousands of folk songs called dainas. Forests cover about half of its land.
standout: Latvia's song and dance festival is one of the largest amateur choral events in the world.
did_you_know: Riga has hundreds of art nouveau buildings. | The first decorated Christmas tree may have stood in Riga in 1510. | Latvia has about 1.2 million collected folk songs.

name: Morocco
about: Morocco is in northwest Africa, with coasts on the Atlantic and Mediterranean. The Atlas Mountains cross it. Markets, mosaics and riads fill cities like Marrakesh and Fez. Tagine and mint tea are favourites.
standout: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez is often cited as the oldest continuously operating university.
did_you_know: Fez has one of the largest car-free urban areas. | Chefchaouen is painted blue. | Argan oil comes from Morocco.

name: Monaco
about: Monaco is a tiny city-state on the Mediterranean coast, surrounded on land by France. Its hillside streets, harbour full of yachts and famous casino in Monte Carlo attract visitors from around the world. The Grimaldi family has ruled it for over 700 years. Every spring, Formula 1 cars race through its narrow streets.
standout: The Monaco Grand Prix has raced through the city's own streets since 1929.
did_you_know: Monaco is the most densely populated country in the world. | Monaco is the second-smallest country, after Vatican City. | Monaco has reclaimed land from the sea, growing by about a fifth since the 1800s.

name: Moldova
about: Moldova is a small, landlocked country between Romania and Ukraine. It has gentle hills, rich black soil and many vineyards. Wine is central to its culture. Orheiul Vechi has a monastery carved into a limestone cliff.
standout: Moldova's Mileștii Mici has one of the largest wine collections in the world, in tunnels underground.
did_you_know: Mileștii Mici's wine cellars stretch for about 200 km. | Moldova is one of the least visited countries in Europe. | Romanian is its official language.

name: Madagascar
about: Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island, in the Indian Ocean off southeast Africa. It split from other land millions of years ago, so most of its plants and animals evolved alone. Lemurs live only here. Its Avenue of the Baobabs is lined with giant trees.
standout: About 90% of Madagascar's wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.
did_you_know: Lemurs are found naturally only in Madagascar. | Madagascar grows much of the world's vanilla. | Six of the world's eight baobab species are native to Madagascar.

name: Maldives
about: The Maldives is a chain of about 1,200 coral islands grouped into atolls in the Indian Ocean, southwest of India. Only around 200 islands are lived on. It is famous for white beaches, clear lagoons and resorts built over the water. Its reefs are home to manta rays, whale sharks and colourful fish.
standout: The Maldives is the world's lowest-lying country, with an average height of about 1.5 m above sea level.
did_you_know: The Maldives is the smallest country in Asia by land area. | Its capital, Malé, is one of the most densely packed cities in the world. | In 2009 its government held a cabinet meeting underwater to draw attention to rising seas.

name: Mexico
about: Mexico lies between the United States and Central America, with coasts on both the Pacific and the Gulf of Mexico. Its land ranges from deserts in the north to volcanoes, rainforests and the Caribbean beaches of the Yucatán. Ancient Maya and Aztec cities still stand across the country. Mexican food, Day of the Dead celebrations and mariachi music are known worldwide.
standout: The Great Pyramid of Cholula is the world's largest pyramid by volume.
did_you_know: Mexico has the largest Spanish-speaking population in the world. | Chocolate, chillies and maize were all first domesticated in Mexico. | Mexico City is built on the bed of the former Lake Texcoco and is slowly sinking.

name: Marshall Islands
about: The Marshall Islands is a Pacific nation of 29 coral atolls. It is very low-lying. Bikini Atoll was used for nuclear tests. Its people navigated with stick charts.
standout: Kwajalein is one of the largest coral atolls in the world.
did_you_know: Stick charts showed ocean swells. | Bikini Atoll gave its name to the swimsuit. | Its average height is about 2 m.

name: North Macedonia
about: North Macedonia is a small, landlocked country in the Balkans, with mountains and deep lakes. Lake Ohrid, shared with Albania, is one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes. The town of Ohrid was once said to have 365 churches. Skopje, its capital, is the birthplace of Mother Teresa.
standout: Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest lakes in Europe, possibly over a million years old.
did_you_know: Lake Ohrid has many species found nowhere else. | Mother Teresa was born in Skopje in 1910. | The country changed its name to North Macedonia in 2019.

name: Mali
about: Mali is a large, landlocked country in West Africa, with the Sahara in the north and the Niger River in the south. It was home to great empires and the city of Timbuktu. Mansa Musa, its medieval ruler, may have been the richest person ever. Its music is world-famous.
standout: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick building in the world.
did_you_know: Timbuktu had famous libraries of manuscripts. | Djenné's mosque is re-plastered each year. | Mansa Musa's pilgrimage made Mali famous.

name: Malta
about: Malta is a small island country in the middle of the Mediterranean, south of Sicily. Its golden stone cities, harbours and forts reflect a long history of knights and sailors. Valletta, the capital, is one of the smallest capitals in the EU. Its ancient temples are among the oldest free-standing buildings on Earth.
standout: Malta's Ġgantija temples are older than Stonehenge and the pyramids of Giza.
did_you_know: Malta has no rivers or lakes that flow all year. | Maltese is the only Semitic language official in the EU. | Malta was awarded the George Cross for bravery in the Second World War.

name: Myanmar
about: Myanmar is the largest country in mainland Southeast Asia, stretching from Himalayan foothills to the Andaman Sea. The Irrawaddy River runs through its heart. Golden pagodas such as Shwedagon in Yangon shine over its cities. Many people wear a long wrapped skirt called a longyi.
standout: Bagan in Myanmar has more than 2,000 surviving Buddhist temples and pagodas on one plain.
did_you_know: Shwedagon Pagoda is covered in gold and topped with thousands of diamonds. | Fishermen on Inle Lake row with one leg wrapped around the oar. | Myanmar is one of the world's biggest sources of jade.

name: Montenegro
about: Montenegro is a small country on the Adriatic, where steep mountains drop straight into the sea. Its name means "Black Mountain". The Bay of Kotor winds inland like a fjord, lined with old stone towns. Lake Skadar is home to pelicans.
standout: The Tara River Canyon is one of the deepest canyons in Europe, about 1,300 m deep.
did_you_know: Montenegro uses the euro without being in the eurozone. | Kotor's old town walls climb the mountain behind it. | The Ostrog Monastery is built into a vertical cliff.

name: Mongolia
about: Mongolia is a vast, landlocked country between Russia and China, made up of grassy steppe, mountains and the Gobi Desert. Many Mongolians still live as nomadic herders in round felt tents called gers. Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire here in the 1200s. The Gobi is famous for its dinosaur fossils and eggs.
standout: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated sovereign country in the world.
did_you_know: Mongolia has more horses than people. | The Naadam festival features wrestling, archery and horse racing. | Ulaanbaatar is the coldest national capital in the world on average.

name: Mozambique
about: Mozambique runs along Africa's southeast coast, with a long Indian Ocean shoreline. Beaches, coral reefs and islands line its coast. The Zambezi River crosses its middle. Its flag is the only one showing a modern rifle.
standout: The Bazaruto Archipelago is one of the last strongholds of the dugong in the western Indian Ocean.
did_you_know: Mozambique Island was once the capital of Portuguese East Africa. | Its flag shows an AK-47. | Whale sharks and manta rays visit Tofo beach.

name: Mauritania
about: Mauritania lies in northwest Africa, mostly in the Sahara. Its coast has rich fishing waters. One of the world's longest trains carries iron ore across its desert. Chinguetti has old libraries.
standout: The Richat Structure, or "Eye of the Sahara", is a 40 km wide rock formation visible from space.
did_you_know: The iron ore train can be about 2.5 km long. | Banc d'Arguin is a huge bird area. | Chinguetti is an ancient trading town.

name: Mauritius
about: Mauritius is an island country in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar. It is surrounded by coral reefs and has a mountainous centre. Its people have Indian, African, Chinese and European roots. The dodo bird lived only here.
standout: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo, which became extinct in the 1600s.
did_you_know: The Seven Coloured Earths are sand dunes of different colours. | Mauritius has no standing army. | An underwater "waterfall" illusion appears off Le Morne.

name: Malawi
about: Malawi is a narrow, landlocked country in southeast Africa, with Lake Malawi along much of its length. It is known as "the warm heart of Africa". Tea and tobacco are grown on its hills. Colourful cichlid fish fill its lake.
standout: Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake in the world.
did_you_know: Lake Malawi has hundreds of cichlid species. | The lake covers about a fifth of the country. | Mount Mulanje rises over 3,000 m.

name: Malaysia
about: Malaysia is split between the Malay Peninsula and the northern part of Borneo, with the South China Sea in between. Rainforests, beaches and modern cities like Kuala Lumpur sit side by side. Malay, Chinese and Indian cultures mix in its food and festivals. Orangutans live in the forests of Sabah and Sarawak.
standout: The Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur are the world's tallest twin skyscrapers.
did_you_know: Rafflesia, found in Malaysia's forests, is one of the largest flowers in the world. | Malaysia has a king who is chosen every five years among nine royal rulers. | Its rainforests are among the oldest on Earth.

name: Namibia
about: Namibia is in southwest Africa, with the Namib Desert along its coast. Its red dunes at Sossusvlei are among the tallest in the world. Etosha has big wildlife. It is one of the least densely populated countries.
standout: The Namib is often called the world's oldest desert.
did_you_know: Sossusvlei has some of the tallest dunes. | Namibia was one of the first to protect its environment in its constitution. | Hoba meteorite is the largest known.

name: Niger
about: Niger is a large, landlocked country in West Africa, mostly Sahara. The Niger River flows through its southwest. The Aïr Mountains hold rock art. Its Wodaabe people hold the Gerewol festival.
standout: Niger's Ténéré is one of the Sahara's largest sand seas.
did_you_know: The Tree of Ténéré was once the most isolated tree on Earth. | Dinosaur fossils have been found in Niger. | Agadez has a famous mud-brick minaret.

name: Nigeria
about: Nigeria sits on West Africa's Gulf of Guinea, stretching from mangrove swamps on the coast to dry savanna in the north. It is Africa's most populous country, with more than 250 ethnic groups and hundreds of languages. Lagos is one of the continent's biggest and busiest cities. Nigerian music, especially Afrobeats, and its films are popular across Africa and far beyond.
standout: Nollywood is one of the world's largest film industries by number of films made each year.
did_you_know: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa. | More than 500 languages are spoken in Nigeria. | Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, releases more films a year than almost any other.

name: Nicaragua
about: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America. It has lakes, volcanoes and two coasts. Granada is a colourful colonial city. Ometepe island has two volcanoes.
standout: Lake Nicaragua has freshwater sharks.
did_you_know: Ometepe has two volcanoes. | Volcano boarding is popular. | Lake Nicaragua is Central America's largest lake.

name: Netherlands
about: The Netherlands is a low, flat country in Western Europe on the North Sea, with about a quarter of it below sea level. Dikes, windmills and canals keep the water out. It is known for tulips, cheese and bicycles. Amsterdam is built on many canals.
standout: The Delta Works are one of the largest flood-protection systems in the world.
did_you_know: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands. | Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea in the 20th century. | The Netherlands is one of the world's largest food exporters.

name: Norway
about: Norway runs along the western side of the Scandinavian Peninsula in northern Europe, with a coastline cut deep by fjords. It also governs the Arctic islands of Svalbard. Mountains, glaciers and northern lights draw visitors from around the world. Oil and gas made Norway one of the richest countries, and Norwegians are famous for cross-country skiing.
standout: The Lærdal Tunnel, 24.5 km long, is the world's longest road tunnel.
did_you_know: In northern Norway the sun does not set for weeks in summer. | Norway's sovereign wealth fund is the largest in the world. | Most new cars sold in Norway are fully electric.

name: Nepal
about: Nepal is a landlocked country in the Himalayas, between India and China. Eight of the world's ten highest mountains rise along its borders. Its lowlands hold jungles with rhinos and tigers, while Kathmandu is full of temples and stupas. Lumbini in Nepal is the birthplace of the Buddha.
standout: Nepal is home to Mount Everest, at 8,849 m the highest mountain on Earth.
did_you_know: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle. | Nepal uses its own calendar, which runs about 56 years ahead of the Western one. | Chitwan National Park is a stronghold of the one-horned rhinoceros.

name: Nauru
about: Nauru is a tiny island in the Pacific. It was mined for phosphate. It has no official capital. You can drive around it in about 20 minutes.
standout: Nauru is the smallest island country in the world.
did_you_know: Nauru has no official capital. | A road circles the island. | It was once very rich from phosphate.

name: New Zealand
about: New Zealand is an island country in the southwest Pacific, made of two main islands. It has mountains, fjords and volcanoes. Māori culture is central. The kiwi bird lives only there.
standout: New Zealand was among the last major landmasses settled by humans.
did_you_know: New Zealand was the first to give women the vote, in 1893. | Kiwis cannot fly. | Hobbit films were shot there.

name: Oman
about: Oman sits on the southeastern corner of the Arabian Peninsula, with a long coast on the Arabian Sea. Rocky mountains, deep canyons and desert dunes cover its land. Oman was a great seafaring nation, trading as far as East Africa. Frankincense, a fragrant resin, has been harvested here for thousands of years.
standout: Majlis al Jinn in Oman is one of the largest known cave chambers in the world.
did_you_know: Oman's southern Dhofar region gets monsoon rain and turns green each summer. | Old falaj water channels still water its farms. | Sea turtles nest on its beaches at Ras al Jinz.

name: Pakistan
about: Pakistan stretches from the Arabian Sea coast up to some of the world's highest mountains in the north. The Indus River runs through its whole length, feeding farms on its plains. It holds the remains of Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation. It is known for cricket, colourful truck art and its food.
standout: K2, on Pakistan's border with China, is the second-highest mountain on Earth at 8,611 m.
did_you_know: The Karakoram Highway is one of the highest paved roads in the world. | Mohenjo-daro had planned streets and drains more than 4,000 years ago. | Pakistan makes many of the world's hand-stitched footballs.

name: Panama
about: Panama connects Central and South America. The Panama Canal cuts across it. It has rainforests and islands. Panama City has a modern skyline.
standout: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
did_you_know: You can see the sun rise over the Pacific in Panama. | The canal opened in 1914. | Panama hats come from Ecuador.

name: Peru
about: Peru is in western South America, with desert coast, Andes and Amazon. It was the heart of the Inca Empire. Its food is famous. Lake Titicaca lies on its border.
standout: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel high in the Andes.
did_you_know: Peru has thousands of potato varieties. | The Nazca Lines are huge desert drawings. | Ceviche is a national dish.

name: Philippines
about: The Philippines is an archipelago of more than 7,000 islands in the western Pacific. Volcanoes, rice terraces and white beaches cover its islands. Its culture blends Asian, Spanish and American influences. It is home to the tiny tarsier, a primate with huge eyes.
standout: The Puerto Princesa Underground River is one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world.
did_you_know: The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved by hand about 2,000 years ago. | Basketball is the most popular sport in the Philippines. | Jeepneys, colourful public buses, began as old army jeeps.

name: Palau
about: Palau is a nation of about 340 islands in the western Pacific. It has coral reefs and rock islands. It created a large shark sanctuary. Visitors sign an eco pledge.
standout: Palau's Jellyfish Lake is home to millions of stingless golden jellyfish.
did_you_know: Palau created one of the first shark sanctuaries. | Rock Islands are a UNESCO site. | Visitors sign an eco pledge.

name: Papua New Guinea
about: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of New Guinea and many islands. It has mountains, rainforests and coral reefs. Birds of paradise live there. It has over 800 languages.
standout: Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages, more than any other country.
did_you_know: PNG has the most languages in the world. | Birds of paradise are on its flag. | The Kokoda Track is famous.

name: Poland
about: Poland is in Central Europe, stretching from the Baltic Sea to the Carpathian Mountains. Its cities, like Kraków and Gdańsk, have rebuilt old towns full of colour. Białowieża Forest is home to Europe's heaviest land animal, the bison. Pierogi dumplings are a favourite food.
standout: The Wieliczka Salt Mine has chapels and statues carved entirely out of salt.
did_you_know: Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw. | Malbork Castle is the largest castle in the world by land area. | Białowieża Forest is one of Europe's last primeval forests.

name: North Korea
about: North Korea occupies the northern half of the Korean Peninsula, a mountainous land bordering China and Russia. It has been ruled by the same family since its founding in 1948 and is one of the most closed countries in the world. Its capital is Pyongyang. Mount Paektu, a volcano on the Chinese border, is the highest point on the peninsula.
standout: Pyongyang's Rungrado May Day Stadium is one of the largest stadiums in the world by capacity.
did_you_know: North Korea uses its own calendar year system, called Juche. | Mount Paektu has a large crater lake called Heaven Lake. | Very few foreign visitors are allowed into the country each year.

name: Portugal
about: Portugal lies on the western edge of the Iberian Peninsula, facing the Atlantic. It also includes the Azores and Madeira islands. Its explorers mapped much of the world's oceans in the 1400s and 1500s. It is famous for tiles, fado music and custard tarts.
standout: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama was the first European to reach India by sea, in 1498.
did_you_know: Portugal produces about half of the world's cork. | Lisbon is older than Rome. | Nazaré has some of the biggest surfable waves in the world.

name: Paraguay
about: Paraguay is a landlocked country in South America. The Paraguay River divides it. Guaraní is widely spoken. Its electricity comes from huge dams.
standout: The Itaipú Dam, shared with Brazil, is one of the largest hydroelectric plants.
did_you_know: Most Paraguayans speak Guaraní. | It exports hydroelectric power. | Ñandutí lace is a tradition.

name: Palestine
about: Palestine includes the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, on the eastern Mediterranean. Its land holds some of the world's most important religious sites, including in Bethlehem and Jerusalem. Olive trees and terraced hills are a large part of its landscape. Palestinian embroidery, called tatreez, is a treasured tradition.
standout: Jericho is often cited as one of the oldest inhabited cities in the world.
did_you_know: Jericho is also one of the lowest cities in the world, below sea level. | Olive oil and olive-wood carving have long been part of the economy. | Tatreez embroidery patterns differ from village to village.

name: Qatar
about: Qatar is a small peninsula sticking into the Persian Gulf from Arabia. Most of it is flat desert, but its capital, Doha, has a skyline of striking modern towers. Natural gas has made it one of the richest countries per person. It hosted the football World Cup in 2022.
standout: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first held in the Arab world.
did_you_know: Qatar has some of the world's largest natural gas reserves. | Khor Al Adaid, the "Inland Sea", is where desert dunes meet the sea. | The Museum of Islamic Art in Doha sits on its own island.

name: Romania
about: Romania is in southeastern Europe, with the Carpathian Mountains curving through its middle. Medieval towns and castles fill Transylvania. The Danube ends in a huge delta on its Black Sea coast. Bran Castle is linked in popular stories to Dracula.
standout: Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.
