did_you_know: The Danube Delta is one of Europe's largest wetlands. | Romania has some of Europe's largest areas of untouched forest. | Romanian is a Romance language, related to Italian and French.

name: Russia
about: Russia stretches across Eastern Europe and northern Asia, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific. It has huge forests, tundra, mountains and frozen Siberian plains. Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, is here. Russian writers, ballet and music are famous worldwide.
standout: Russia is the largest country in the world, covering about one-eighth of Earth's land.
did_you_know: The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world. | Lake Baikal holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. | Russia spans 11 time zones.

name: Rwanda
about: Rwanda is a small, landlocked country in East Africa, called "the land of a thousand hills". Its green hills grow tea and coffee. It is one of the few places to see mountain gorillas. Kigali is known as one of Africa's cleanest cities.
standout: Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park is home to mountain gorillas.
did_you_know: Plastic bags have been banned in Rwanda since 2008. | Rwanda has a high share of women in its parliament. | Umuganda is a monthly national community work day.

name: Saudi Arabia
about: Saudi Arabia covers most of the Arabian Peninsula, between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. Most of it is desert, but it holds huge oil reserves. Mecca and Medina, the two holiest cities in Islam, are here. Every year, millions of Muslims travel to Mecca for the Hajj pilgrimage.
standout: The Rub' al Khali in Saudi Arabia is the largest continuous sand desert in the world.
did_you_know: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers. | Hegra, an ancient Nabataean city, has tombs carved into rock. | Camels have long been central to life in the desert.

name: Sudan
about: Sudan is in northeast Africa, where the Blue and White Nile meet at Khartoum. Most of it is desert or dry savanna. Ancient Nubian kingdoms built pyramids here. It is a top gum arabic producer.
standout: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt, at sites like Meroë.
did_you_know: Sudan has about 200 pyramids. | The two Niles meet at Khartoum. | Sudan produces much of the world's gum arabic.

name: Senegal
about: Senegal is the westernmost country of mainland Africa. Dakar, its capital, sits on a peninsula. It is known for music, wrestling and teranga, meaning hospitality. Gorée Island is a memorial to the slave trade.
standout: Lake Retba, or Lac Rose, turns pink because of salt-loving algae.
did_you_know: Senegalese wrestling is hugely popular. | Lac Rose looks pink. | The African Renaissance Monument is taller than the Statue of Liberty.

name: Singapore
about: Singapore is a small island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula. It grew from a trading port into one of the world's busiest harbours and financial centres. Its people speak English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil, and its street food is famous. Gardens by the Bay has giant metal "supertrees" covered in plants.
standout: Singapore's Changi Airport has the world's tallest indoor waterfall, the Rain Vortex.
did_you_know: Singapore has grown by about a quarter by reclaiming land from the sea. | Chewing gum sales have been banned since 1992. | It is one of only three city-states in the world.

name: Solomon Islands
about: Solomon Islands is a Pacific country of nearly 1,000 islands. It has rainforests and coral lagoons. Many WWII wrecks lie in its waters. Shell money is a tradition.
standout: Marovo Lagoon is one of the largest saltwater lagoons in the world.
did_you_know: Shell money is still used in ceremonies. | Iron Bottom Sound has many shipwrecks. | It has many languages.

name: Sierra Leone
about: Sierra Leone is on West Africa's coast, with beaches, mountains and rainforest. Freetown has one of the largest natural harbours in the world. It has rich mineral deposits. Its name means "Lion Mountains".
standout: Sierra Leone's Tiwai Island is one of the richest primate habitats in Africa.
did_you_know: Freetown's harbour is among the largest natural harbours. | Sierra Leone is known for diamonds. | Tiwai has many primate species.

name: El Salvador
about: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America. It has volcanoes and Pacific beaches. Surfing is popular. Pupusas are its national dish.
standout: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America by area.
did_you_know: El Salvador adopted bitcoin as legal tender in 2021. | Pupusas are its national dish. | It has over 20 volcanoes.

name: San Marino
about: San Marino is a tiny country on the slopes of Mount Titano, surrounded entirely by Italy. Its three medieval towers sit on the mountain's peaks. It has its own government, stamps and coins. Its people have kept their independence for centuries.
standout: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301.
did_you_know: San Marino has two heads of state, the Captains Regent, who serve six months. | Its constitution, from 1600, is among the oldest still in use. | There are more cars than people in San Marino.

name: Somalia
about: Somalia sits on the Horn of Africa and has the longest coastline in mainland Africa. Most of its land is dry plains. Camel herding is a big part of life. Somali poetry has a strong oral tradition.
standout: Las Geel caves in the Somali region hold some of Africa's best-preserved ancient rock paintings.
did_you_know: Somalia has one of the largest camel populations in the world. | Somalia is sometimes called a "nation of poets". | Its coastline is about 3,000 km long.

name: Serbia
about: Serbia is a landlocked country in the Balkans, with flat farmland in the north and mountains in the south. The Danube and Sava rivers meet at its capital, Belgrade. Its monasteries have old painted walls. Serbia is famous for tennis players and raspberries.
standout: The Iron Gates gorge on the Danube is one of the largest river gorges in Europe.
did_you_know: Serbia is one of the world's largest raspberry exporters. | Nikola Tesla was of Serbian origin. | Belgrade is one of the oldest cities in Europe.

name: South Sudan
about: South Sudan is a landlocked country in East-Central Africa and the world's newest country, independent since 2011. The White Nile flows through its centre, forming the Sudd, one of the world's largest wetlands. Many of its people herd cattle. Its capital is Juba.
standout: South Sudan hosts one of the largest land mammal migrations, of antelopes across its grasslands.
did_you_know: South Sudan became independent on 9 July 2011. | The Sudd wetland can cover tens of thousands of square kilometres. | Cattle are central to many South Sudanese cultures.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
about: São Tomé and Príncipe is a small island country in the Gulf of Guinea, off Central Africa. Its two main islands are volcanic and covered in rainforest. It was once a top cocoa producer. Many plants and birds there are found nowhere else.
standout: Pico Cão Grande is a dramatic volcanic spire rising about 300 m above the jungle.
did_you_know: The equator passes through an islet just south of São Tomé. | It is Africa's second-smallest country by population. | Its cocoa is prized by chocolate makers.

name: Suriname
about: Suriname is on South America's north coast. Most of it is rainforest. Dutch is its official language. Its capital has wooden colonial buildings.
standout: Suriname is the most forested country in the world by share of land.
did_you_know: Suriname is mostly forest. | Dutch is official. | Paramaribo is a UNESCO city.

name: Slovakia
about: Slovakia is a small, landlocked country in Central Europe, with the High Tatras mountains in the north. Its villages keep traditional wooden churches and folk costumes. Spiš Castle is one of Central Europe's biggest castle ruins. Bratislava sits on the Danube near Austria and Hungary.
standout: Slovakia has one of the highest numbers of castles and chateaux per person in the world.
did_you_know: Bratislava borders two countries, Austria and Hungary. | The Dobšiná Ice Cave holds ice all year. | Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country.

name: Slovenia
about: Slovenia is a small country where the Alps, the Mediterranean and the Pannonian plain meet. More than half of it is forest. Lake Bled, with a church on its island, is one of Europe's most photographed places. It has a short but busy Adriatic coast.
standout: The Postojna Cave system has more than 24 km of passages and a cave railway.
did_you_know: The olm, a blind cave salamander, can live for about 100 years. | Slovenia has over 10,000 caves. | Lipizzaner horses come from Lipica in Slovenia.

name: Sweden
about: Sweden is a long Nordic country in northern Europe, with forests, lakes and a coast of many islands. Its north has reindeer herding and the midnight sun. It is known for design, music and the Nobel Prizes. Stockholm is built on 14 islands.
standout: The Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi was the world's first hotel built entirely of ice and snow.
did_you_know: Alfred Nobel, who founded the Nobel Prizes, was Swedish. | Sweden has about 267,000 islands. | Anyone may walk and camp on most land under the "right of public access".

name: Eswatini
about: Eswatini is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa. It has mountains, savanna and reserves with rhinos. Its Umhlanga reed dance is a famous festival. It was formerly called Swaziland.
standout: Eswatini is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world.
did_you_know: Eswatini changed its name in 2018. | Umhlanga reed dance gathers thousands. | It has two capitals.

name: Seychelles
about: Seychelles is a group of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar. Its granite islands are among the oldest ocean islands on Earth. It has white beaches with giant boulders. Aldabra is home to tens of thousands of giant tortoises.
standout: The coco de mer palm of the Seychelles has the largest seed of any plant.
did_you_know: Seychelles has the smallest population of any African country. | Aldabra has one of the largest giant tortoise populations. | Coco de mer seeds can weigh up to 25 kg.

name: Syria
about: Syria lies on the eastern Mediterranean, with a fertile coast, mountains and a large dry interior. Its cities, such as Damascus and Aleppo, have been lived in for thousands of years. Ancient sites like Palmyra and the Crusader castle Krak des Chevaliers stand on its land. Damascus steel was once famous across the world.
standout: Damascus is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
did_you_know: Aleppo soap, made from olive and laurel oil, has been produced for centuries. | Krak des Chevaliers is one of the best-preserved medieval castles. | Ugarit, in Syria, used one of the earliest alphabets.

name: Chad
about: Chad is a large, landlocked country in north-central Africa. Its north is Sahara Desert, its middle is dry Sahel and its south is savanna. The Ennedi Plateau has dramatic rock arches and ancient rock art. Lake Chad gave the country its name.
standout: Lake Chad has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s.
did_you_know: The Ennedi Plateau has natural rock arches over 100 m high. | Chad has more than 120 languages. | Tibesti's Emi Koussi is the highest point in the Sahara.

name: Togo
about: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa. Its coast has lagoons and palm trees. Koutammakou has unique mud tower-houses. Lomé has a big market.
standout: Togo is one of the narrowest countries in Africa, under 120 km wide.
did_you_know: Koutammakou houses are on UNESCO's list. | Lomé's market is famous. | Togo stretches about 600 km north–south.

name: Thailand
about: Thailand lies in the middle of mainland Southeast Asia, with mountains in the north and tropical islands in the south. Golden temples, floating markets and busy Bangkok draw millions of visitors. Thai food, with its mix of sweet, sour, salty and spicy, is loved worldwide. Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonised by a European power.
standout: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is the longest place name in the world.
did_you_know: The Asian elephant is a national symbol of Thailand. | Muay Thai, or Thai boxing, uses fists, elbows, knees and shins. | Songkran, the Thai New Year, is celebrated with giant water fights.

name: Tajikistan
about: Tajikistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia, and more than nine-tenths of it is mountains. The Pamirs, called the "Roof of the World", cover its east. Its people speak Tajik, a form of Persian. The Pamir Highway is one of the highest roads on Earth.
standout: The Fedchenko Glacier is one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.
did_you_know: The Nurek Dam is one of the tallest dams in the world. | Ismoil Somoni Peak is its highest point, at 7,495 m. | Tajik embroidery called suzani decorates homes and weddings.

name: Turkmenistan
about: Turkmenistan is a desert country in Central Asia, with the Karakum Desert covering most of its land. It has some of the world's largest natural gas reserves. Its people are known for fine carpets and the elegant Akhal-Teke horse. Its capital, Ashgabat, is covered in white marble buildings.
standout: The Darvaza gas crater, called the "Door to Hell", has been burning since 1971.
did_you_know: Ashgabat holds a record for the most white marble buildings. | The Akhal-Teke horse has a shiny, metallic-looking coat. | Turkmen carpet designs appear on the national flag.

name: Timor-Leste
about: Timor-Leste occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor, plus a few small islands, north of Australia. It became independent in 2002, making it one of the world's newest countries. Its mountains grow coffee, and its coral reefs are among the richest on Earth. Portuguese and Tetum are its official languages.
standout: The seas around Timor-Leste's Atauro Island have some of the highest reef fish diversity measured anywhere.
did_you_know: Timor-Leste was the first new sovereign country of the 21st century. | It uses the US dollar as its currency. | Its capital, Dili, has a giant statue of Christ overlooking the sea.

name: Tonga
about: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom of 170 islands. It has beaches and coral reefs. Humpback whales visit to breed. It is one of the first to see each new day.
standout: Tonga is the only Pacific nation never colonised.
did_you_know: Tonga is a kingdom. | Humpback whales visit. | Rugby is popular.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
about: Trinidad and Tobago is a Caribbean nation near Venezuela. Its Carnival is famous. The steelpan was invented here. Pitch Lake is the largest natural asphalt lake.
standout: Trinidad and Tobago invented the steelpan, the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century.
did_you_know: Pitch Lake is the largest natural asphalt deposit. | Calypso and soca come from here. | Tobago has coral reefs.

name: Tunisia
about: Tunisia is the northernmost country in Africa, with a Mediterranean coast and the Sahara in the south. Carthage, near Tunis, was a powerful ancient city. Its desert has sets used in famous films. Couscous and harissa are favourites.
standout: The amphitheatre of El Jem is one of the largest Roman amphitheatres in the world.
did_you_know: Matmata's underground houses were used as film sets. | Carthage rivalled Rome. | Chott el Djerid is a vast salt lake.

name: Türkiye
about: Türkiye spans two continents, with most of its land in Asia and a small part in Europe. Istanbul sits on both sides of the Bosphorus strait. It has ancient cities, fairy-chimney rock towers in Cappadocia and long coastlines on four seas. Turkish coffee, tea and sweets like baklava are famous worldwide.
standout: Göbekli Tepe, about 11,000 years old, is one of the oldest known monumental temples.
did_you_know: Istanbul is one of the few major cities that lies on two continents. | Tulips were grown in the Ottoman Empire before they became popular in the Netherlands. | Santa's inspiration, Saint Nicholas, lived in Myra, in today's Türkiye.

name: Tuvalu
about: Tuvalu is a small Polynesian nation of nine islands. It is threatened by rising seas. Its ".tv" domain earns income. It is one of the least visited countries.
standout: Tuvalu is one of the lowest-lying countries, highest point about 4.6 m.
did_you_know: Its ".tv" domain brings in money. | Its highest point is about 4.6 m. | It is one of the smallest countries.

name: Tanzania
about: Tanzania is in East Africa, with the Indian Ocean coast and islands like Zanzibar. It has Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti plains. The Great Migration of wildebeest crosses its parks. Swahili is its national language.
standout: Kilimanjaro, at 5,895 m, is the highest mountain in Africa.
did_you_know: Ngorongoro Crater is the world's largest unbroken volcanic caldera. | Zanzibar is famous for spices. | Tanzania borders three great lakes.

name: Uganda
about: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, around the north of Lake Victoria. It is called "the Pearl of Africa" for its green landscapes. It shelters mountain gorillas and chimpanzees. The Rwenzori Mountains have glaciers near the equator.
standout: The Nile flows out of Lake Victoria at Jinja, in Uganda.
did_you_know: Uganda has about half of the world's mountain gorillas. | Murchison Falls squeezes the Nile through a 7 m gap. | Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake.

name: Ukraine
about: Ukraine is the largest country entirely in Europe, with rich black farmland, the Carpathian Mountains and a coast on the Black Sea. It is one of the world's biggest grain producers. Kyiv has golden-domed churches more than a thousand years old. Painted Easter eggs called pysanky are a Ukrainian tradition.
standout: The Arsenalna station in Kyiv is one of the deepest metro stations in the world.
did_you_know: Ukraine is one of the world's largest sunflower oil producers. | Borscht, a beetroot soup, is a national dish. | The Antonov An-225 was built in Ukraine.

name: Uruguay
about: Uruguay is a small country between Brazil and Argentina. It has beaches and grasslands. It is known for beef and mate. Montevideo is the capital.
standout: Uruguay won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.
did_you_know: Uruguay hosted the first World Cup. | Mate tea is widely drunk. | Most of its electricity is renewable.

name: United States
about: The United States stretches across North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific, plus Alaska and Hawaii. It has deserts, mountains, forests and big cities. It is a world leader in technology and film. The Grand Canyon is one of its famous sights.
standout: Yellowstone, created in 1872, was the world's first national park.
did_you_know: The US has no official language at the federal level. | Alaska's Denali is North America's highest peak. | Hawaii is still growing from volcanic eruptions.

name: Uzbekistan
about: Uzbekistan lies in the heart of Central Asia and is one of only two doubly landlocked countries. Its cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva were stops on the Silk Road. Blue-tiled domes and minarets rise above their old towns. Plov, rice cooked with meat and carrots, is its national dish.
standout: Samarkand's Registan square is one of the great architectural ensembles of the Islamic world.
did_you_know: Uzbekistan is one of the world's two doubly landlocked countries, with Liechtenstein. | The Aral Sea, on its border, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s. | Al-Khwarizmi, whose name gave us the word "algorithm", came from this region.

name: Vatican City
about: Vatican City is a tiny walled country inside the city of Rome, Italy. It is the home of the Pope and the centre of the Catholic Church. St Peter's Basilica and the Sistine Chapel, with Michelangelo's painted ceiling, are among its treasures. Fewer than a thousand people live there, but millions of visitors come every year.
standout: Vatican City is the only country whose entire territory is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
did_you_know: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, at about 0.44 km². | The Vatican is protected by the Swiss Guard, founded in 1506. | The whole country could fit inside New York's Central Park about eight times.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
about: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a Caribbean country of one main island and many small ones. It has volcanoes, beaches and sailing waters. Tobago Cays is a marine park. Its botanic gardens are among the oldest in the Americas.
standout: La Soufrière on St Vincent erupted in 2021.
did_you_know: Its botanic garden dates from 1765. | Tobago Cays has sea turtles. | The Grenadines have about 32 islands.

name: Venezuela
about: Venezuela is on South America's north coast. It has Caribbean beaches, the Andes and flat-topped mountains called tepuis. Angel Falls is here. It has large oil reserves.
standout: Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, at 979 m.
did_you_know: Catatumbo lightning strikes very often. | Tepuis inspired lost-world stories. | Venezuela has huge oil reserves.

name: Vietnam
about: Vietnam is a long, S-shaped country along the eastern edge of mainland Southeast Asia. Its north has limestone peaks like those of Ha Long Bay, and its south has the green Mekong Delta. Busy cities such as Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City are filled with motorbikes and street food. Pho noodle soup is its best-known dish.
standout: Son Doong in Vietnam is the world's largest known cave passage.
did_you_know: Vietnam is one of the world's largest coffee exporters. | Ha Long Bay has about 1,600 limestone islands and islets. | Water puppetry, performed on a pool, is a centuries-old Vietnamese art.

name: Vanuatu
about: Vanuatu is a chain of about 80 islands in the South Pacific. It has active volcanoes. Land diving is a tradition. It has many languages.
standout: Land diving on Pentecost Island inspired bungee jumping.
did_you_know: Mount Yasur volcano can be visited. | Land diving inspired bungee jumping. | Vanuatu has an underwater post office.

name: Samoa
about: Samoa is a Polynesian island nation. It has rainforests and beaches. Its culture follows fa'a Samoa. Tattoo traditions are important.
standout: Samoa moved across the International Date Line in 2011, skipping a day.
did_you_know: Samoa skipped 30 December 2011. | Tattoo comes from Samoan "tatau". | To Sua Ocean Trench is famous.

name: Yemen
about: Yemen lies at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, with mountains, deserts and coasts on the Red Sea and Arabian Sea. Its old cities have tall houses built of mud brick and decorated windows. Coffee was first traded widely from its port of Mocha. Its island of Socotra has trees found nowhere else.
standout: Shibam's mud-brick tower houses have earned it the nickname "Manhattan of the desert".
did_you_know: The "mocha" in coffee names comes from Yemen's port city. | Socotra's dragon's blood trees look like giant umbrellas. | Sana'a's old city has been lived in for over 2,500 years.

name: South Africa
about: South Africa is at the southern tip of Africa, where the Atlantic and Indian Oceans meet. Its land ranges from Table Mountain and the Cape winelands to dry Karoo plains and the savanna of Kruger National Park. It has 12 official languages and three capital cities. It is one of the best places in the world to see lions, elephants and rhinos.
standout: The Cradle of Humankind holds some of the world's richest finds of early human fossils.
did_you_know: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. | South Africa has 12 official languages, including sign language. | South Africa completely surrounds the country of Lesotho.

name: Zambia
about: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa, with high plateaus and big rivers. It shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe. Its national parks have huge herds of wildlife. Copper mining is its main industry.
standout: Victoria Falls, shared with Zimbabwe, is the largest sheet of falling water in the world.
did_you_know: Victoria Falls is known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya. | Kasanka hosts a big fruit-bat migration. | Zambia is one of Africa's largest copper producers.

name: Zimbabwe
about: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa, between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers. It shares Victoria Falls with Zambia. It has huge granite boulders and the ruins of Great Zimbabwe. It has 16 official languages.
standout: Great Zimbabwe was the largest stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa before 1500.
did_you_know: Zimbabwe has 16 official languages. | Lake Kariba is one of the largest artificial lakes. | The country is named after Great Zimbabwe.
